categories.title: Power tools
categories.blurb: Drills, drivers, saws, grinders and accessories.

categories.title: Hand tools
categories.blurb: Spanners, screwdrivers, pliers, hammers and bit sets.

guide.p: Locking C-clamps and pipe clamp heads hold stock still so cuts stay straight. Grab a pack when you clamp several pieces at once.
A 150mm bench vise with anvil grips pipe, plate and odd shapes while you file, tap or hammer. Bolt it to a solid workbench.
Heavy-duty bolt cutters snip padlocks, chain and wire. A thread repair kit restores stripped M5–M12 holes without replacing the whole part.

categories.title: Hardware & fasteners
categories.blurb: Screws, bolts, anchors, hinges and fixings.

guide.p: Bolt a castor to each corner, with the braked pair at one end. Check the total load rating covers the bench plus tools.
Measure the cabinet depth and pick runners that match it. Full-extension runners let you reach the back of every drawer.
Barrel bolts give a simple lock for sheds, gates and cupboard doors. Stainless steel suits outdoor use.
A wall key safe lets trades or family get in without you home. Mount it out of plain sight.

categories.title: Building & construction
categories.blurb: Sawhorses, clamps, ladders and site gear.

guide.p: A step stool suits quick jobs at home, like shelves and light fittings. For gutters, painting or ceilings, pick a taller ladder.
A platform ladder with handrails gives you something to hold while both hands work. Always set it on firm, level ground.
An install kit keeps boards tight and spacing even along the walls. Check the board maker's own fitting guide first.
A heavy-duty tarp keeps rain off timber, tools and open roofs. Tie it down at every eyelet in wind.

categories.title: Workshop storage
categories.blurb: Tool chests, workbenches, trolleys and racking.

guide.p: Steel shelving suits heavy boxes and tools in the garage. Wire shelving lets air through and is easy to wipe down. Check each listing for the rated load per shelf.
Slatwall panels and wall hooks hold tools, hoses and leads where you can see them. A ceiling hoist frees up floor space for the car.
Drawer cabinets keep screws, bolts and fittings sorted by size. Pick more drawers if you keep lots of small parts.

categories.title: Automotive & 4WD
categories.blurb: Upgrades for older cars, 4WD and recovery gear, towing, caravan and car care.

guide.p: Lower tyre pressure gives more grip on sand and rough tracks. Pack deflators to let air out evenly and a 12V compressor to pump back up before the bitumen.
Recovery tracks help when you bog in sand or mud. A jump starter gets a flat battery going without a second car.
Check your roof type first: some bars clamp to rails, others fit cars without rails. Check the listing's bar length and load rating against your car's roof limit.
A dash cam records the road ahead and behind. A mirror monitor kit adds a reversing camera to older cars.

categories.title: Garden & outdoor
categories.blurb: Pruners, rakes, hoses and outdoor gear.

guide.p: An expandable hose shrinks back when the tap is off, so it stores in a bucket. Drain it after use and keep it out of hot sun.
Lay woven weed mat over cleared soil, overlap the joins and pin it down. Cover it with mulch or pebbles so it lasts longer.
Edging keeps lawn out of garden beds and mulch off paths. Dig a narrow trench, set the edge level with the grass, then backfill.
A kneeler pad cushions weeding time. Flip it over and it becomes a low seat for planting.

categories.title: BBQ & Camping
categories.blurb: BBQs, smokers, tents, camp furniture, lighting and portable fridges.

guide.p: Grill fast over direct heat on a charcoal BBQ. Smoke low and slow in a smoker. A thermometer takes the guesswork out of both.
Pick one size up from your group so there’s room for bags. Instant-up tents are quickest to pitch.
A cooler box suits day trips. For longer trips, a 12V fridge freezer keeps food cold without ice.

categories.title: Safety & workwear
categories.blurb: Gloves, glasses, hearing protection and hi-vis.

guide.p: Gel knee pads spread the load when tiling, concreting or weeding. Check the straps sit above and below the joint, not on it.
Reflective tape marks trailers, posts, steps and hazards so they show up in headlights. Clean and dry the surface before you stick it.
Cones with reflective bands close off a driveway, work zone or wet floor fast. Stackable sets store flat in a ute or shed.

categories.title: Music gear
categories.blurb: Stands, mics, studio foam, rack gear and stage essentials.

guide.p: Start with one good dynamic mic on a solid boom stand. A small isolation shield cuts room echo while you record.
Put foam panels at ear height beside and behind you. Bass traps go in the corners, where low end builds up.
An X-frame folds flat and suits gigs. A Z-style stand is steadier and leaves room for your legs.
Raise speakers to ear height with stands. Cover floor cables with a ramp, and lock small gear in a rack drawer.
